rows.name: TRON_NIX_LINT_SHELL
rows.who_sets: The Nix lint shell and the Nix `lefthook` wrapper (`flake.nix`).
rows.values: Only the exact text `1` turns it on. Any other text counts as off.
rows.default: Unset: off. The hook commands try `ci/.venv/bin/ruff` and `ci/.venv/bin/python` first, then the tools on `PATH`.
rows.effect: With `1`, the Lefthook (Git hook runner) commands `ruff-format`, `ruff-check` and `agent-guidance` run `ruff` and `python3` from `PATH` and do not look in `ci/.venv/bin`. `bin/ci/lint-ci-pins.sh` does the same for `python3`. A missing `nixfmt` is an error and not a skip.
rows.notes: `flake.nix` sets `1` in the Nix lint shell (`nix develop .#lint`) and in the `lefthook` wrapper script of the Nix shells. `bin/ci/test-nix-lint-toolchain.sh` fails when the value is not `1`. Without `1`, a missing `nixfmt` is skipped unless `CI` is set.

rows.name: TRON_PERFETTO_CONFIG
rows.values: Path of a Perfetto config file in protobuf text format. A path that starts with `/` is used as written. Any other path is relative to the repository root.
rows.default: Unset: `tronperf` uses `perfetto/runtron.cfg` as the base config. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: `tronperf` (the Perfetto launcher for runtron) uses the file as its base config. `perfetto/generate-config` applies the command-line options of `tronperf` on top of it.
rows.notes: The option `--perfetto-config` overrides it. `perfetto/wrapper` does not read it.

rows.name: TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT
rows.values: Whole seconds from `1` to `30`, as 1 or 2 decimal digits. `08` means 8 seconds. Any other text stops the launcher with exit status 2.
rows.default: Unset: 30 seconds. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: Sets the longest time that `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the 2 Perfetto launchers) wait for each readiness signal. The signals come from `traced` and `traced_probes` (the 2 Perfetto daemons) and from the `perfetto` client.
rows.notes: When a wait reaches the limit, the launcher prints an error and exits with a non-zero status. The error for a rejected value is `TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT must be an integer from 1 to 30`.

rows.name: TRON_PERFETTO_SCHEMA_DIR
rows.who_sets: The Nix dev shell and the `nix run` apps `tronperf`, `wrapper`.
rows.values: Path of a directory that holds the generated Python module `perfetto_config_pb2` and the file `perfetto_schema_release.txt`.
rows.default: Unset: the Python module search path is not changed. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: `perfetto/generate-config` (the script that builds the Perfetto config for `tronperf` and `wrapper`) puts the directory first on the Python module search path. It then imports `perfetto_config_pb2`.
rows.notes: `generate-config` exits with an error when the import fails. It also exits when `perfetto_schema_release.txt` beside the imported module is missing or does not hold `57.2`. `perfetto/test_perfetto.py` reads the variable in the same way.

rows.name: TRON_RUNTRON
rows.values: Path of a runtron executable. The text is used as the command. `tronperf` does not check it.
rows.default: Unset: `gen/runtron` under the repository root. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: `tronperf` (the Perfetto launcher for runtron) starts this program with `--trace traced` after the Perfetto session is ready. With the option `--gen`, it passes `--trace-gen traced`.

rows.name: TRON_TP_ADDR
rows.values: `HOST:PORT` of a running `trace_processor_shell --httpd` server, for example `127.0.0.1:9001`. The text is passed unchanged to the Perfetto Python package.
rows.default: Unset: no default address. Without a trace path and without `--addr`, the script prints an error and exits with status 2.
rows.effect: The script connects to that trace processor server (`trace_processor_shell`, the Perfetto program that runs SQL queries on a trace). It does not load a trace file. It does not use `--bin-path` or `TRON_TP_BIN` then.
rows.notes: The script reads it only when the command line has no trace path and no `--addr` option. With a trace path, the script loads the trace itself and ignores the variable. An empty value counts as unset.

evidence.quote: if addr is None and not args.trace:
if not addr and not args.trace:

rows.name: TRON_TP_BIN
rows.values: Path of an executable `trace_processor_shell` (the Perfetto program that runs SQL queries on a trace). The Python scripts expand a leading `~`.
rows.default: Unset: `analyze_kv_duration` exits with status 2. The 2 `tron_*.py` scripts do the same without `--bin-path`. `rinzler-capture.sh` skips its trace summary.
rows.effect: The Python scripts pass the path as `bin_path` to the Perfetto Python package to load a trace. `perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh` runs the program 4 times after a capture and prints a summary of the trace.
rows.notes: The option `--bin-path` of the 2 `tron_*.py` scripts overrides it. A path that is not an executable file makes the Python scripts exit with status 2. `tron_trace_query.py` does not use it in `--addr` mode. Outside `x86_64-linux` the Nix dev shell sets an empty value.

evidence.quote: echo "(TRON_TP_BIN unset; run inside nix develop for a capture summary)"

rows.name: TRON_TRACEFS
rows.who_sets: Nothing in TRON, except one test in `perfetto/test_perfetto.py`.
rows.values: Only the exact text `/sys/kernel/tracing` is accepted. Any other non-empty text stops the launcher with an error and exit status 2.
rows.default: Unset: accepted. An empty value is also accepted.
rows.effect: The variable does not select a tracefs (Linux kernel tracing file system) directory. `tronperf` and `wrapper` (the 2 Perfetto launchers) always use `/sys/kernel/tracing`. They only reject a different value.
rows.notes: The error message names `TRON_TRACEFS` and the required path.

evidence.quote: error "TRON_TRACEFS must be $DEFAULT_TRACEFS because traced_probes uses that path"

rows.name: UV
rows.who_sets: CI workflows. A developer, to select another `uv`.
rows.values: Command name or path of `uv` (the Python package manager that the repository uses). The text is used as the command.
rows.default: Unset: `make` and the CI scripts run `uv` from `PATH`. The Python scripts try `PATH`, then `/tools/uv/uv`. Empty: `make` keeps the empty text.
rows.effect: `make` runs it for the `*-deps` targets, `python-lock` and the `gen/tokenize_py` build. `ingest/build-model.py` and `bin/extract_logits` run it to start the export scripts of `ingest/export`. CI steps run `$UV sync` to install Python environments, and 2 CI scripts run `bin/ci/benchmark_info.py` with it.
rows.notes: With an empty value, the `make` recipes have no program name. The other readers treat an empty value as unset. `ingest/build-model.py` runs no `uv` with `--export-with-current-python` or with a non-empty `IN_NIX_SHELL`. CI workflows write `UV=/tools/uv/<version>/uv` to `GITHUB_ENV`.

rows.name: VERBOSE
rows.values: `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh`: only the exact text `true` turns it on. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh`: any non-empty text turns it on.
rows.default: Unset: off in both scripts. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh` (the request generator for Perfetto captures) prints the text of each model response. `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` (the Rust version check and setup script) prints its information messages.
rows.notes: The 2 scripts are not related. In `burst-test.sh`, the option `-v` or `--verbose` sets it to `true`. CMake runs `rust/rust-toolchain.sh` at configure time and prints its output. An exported value adds the messages there.

rows.name: WEIGHTS
rows.values: Path of model weights. The text is passed unchanged as the `--default-weights` argument of `ingest/build-model.py`.
rows.default: Unset: the script passes no `--default-weights` for a model whose registry entry has no `default_weights`. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: For each model whose entry in the model registry (`config/models.yaml`) has no `default_weights`, `ingest/build-all.sh` passes the value as `--default-weights` to `ingest/build-model.py`. For the other models it passes the registry value.
rows.notes: `ingest/build-model.py` uses `--default-weights` only when it adds a model configuration entry. It adds none with `--no-config`. `build-all.sh` passes `--no-config` for each model that has an architecture name in the registry. The value then changes nothing.

rows.name: WEIGHTS_ROOT
rows.who_sets: A developer, by hand. `config/test_model_definitions.py` sets it in one test.
rows.values: Path of a directory. It holds one sub-directory of model weights for each Hugging Face model ID.
rows.default: Unset: `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: `ingest/build-all.sh` passes `<WEIGHTS_ROOT>/<model ID>` to `ingest/build-model.py` as the model path (`-m`). A model whose directory does not exist fails with `local weights not found`.
rows.notes: A failure of a required model ends the script. A failure of an optional model is only reported. `ingest/build-model.py` does not read the variable. It has its own fixed path `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface`.

evidence.quote: echo "=== $(red Error): $(blue $model) local weights not found at $local_path"

rows.name: WINDOW_MS
rows.values: Whole number of milliseconds. The script uses the text in bash arithmetic and does not validate it.
rows.default: Unset: 5000 milliseconds (5 seconds). An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: Sets the arrival window of `perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh` (the request generator for Perfetto captures). Each request starts at a random offset from 0 milliseconds to less than this value.

rows.name: pci_id
rows.values: Text of the form `vvvv:dddd`: a PCI vendor ID of 4 hex digits, a colon, and a device ID of 4 hex digits. The script passes it unquoted to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh`.
rows.default: Unset: `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` gets only the card address. It prints a warning and continues without the ID check.
rows.effect: In bind mode, `bin/bind-cards.sh` passes the value to `bin/vfio_pci_bind.sh` for each FPGA card. That script checks that a device with this vendor and device ID is at the card address before it binds the card to `vfio-pci` (the Linux driver for user-space access to a PCI device).
rows.notes: The script never assigns `pci_id`. The value comes from the environment. Unbind mode (first argument `unbind`) does not use it. Text in another form, such as `8200:`, stops the script with an error. Text in the form of a PCI address replaces the card address.

evidence.quote: echo "Error: Vendor:Device ${VD} not found at ${BDF}, unable to bind device" 1>&2
echo "Warning: You did not specify a Vendor:Device (vvvv:dddd), unable to validate ${BDF}" 1>&2

rows.name: start_address
rows.values: Offset from the base address, as hexadecimal digits without the `0x` prefix. The script adds `0x` in front and uses the text in bash arithmetic without a check.
rows.default: Unset: the offset counts as 0. The first address is the base address `0x37000000000`. An empty value does the same.
rows.effect: `bin/iotools-1.5/fpga_bist_1.sh` uses `start_address` before it assigns it. On the first pass of its loop it adds the inherited value to the base address `0x37000000000`. It writes a test pattern to that memory address with `./iotools mmio_write64` and reads it back.
rows.notes: Each later pass adds the address of the previous pass to the base address again. The script reads the address column of `address_map_1.csv` and does not use it.

evidence.quote: while IFS=, read -r name _ _ _ range _; do

new_terms.definition: The launcher `perfetto/tronperf`. It starts a Perfetto session and then runs runtron with tracing turned on.
The launcher `perfetto/wrapper`. It starts a Perfetto session and can signal a running process, such as rinzler, to emit trace events.
The 2 Perfetto daemons that the launchers start before the `perfetto` client.
The Perfetto program `trace_processor_shell`. It loads a trace file and runs SQL queries on it.
The Linux kernel tracing file system, mounted at `/sys/kernel/tracing`.
The Git hook runner that runs the lint commands of `lefthook.yml` before a commit.
The development environment that `nix develop .#lint` starts. It holds the pinned lint tools.
The Python package manager that the repository uses to install its pinned Python environments.
The file `config/models.yaml`. It lists the models that TRON supports.
The Linux driver that gives a user program direct access to a PCI device, such as an FPGA card.

notes: All 15 names are kept. `pci_id` and `start_address` are lower-case shell names that their scripts use and never assign first, so the scripts take them from the environment. No file in the checkout sets or documents them. `VERBOSE` has 2 unrelated readers and is filed under load-test with the other `burst-test.sh` variables. `UV` has readers in make, ingest and CI, and is filed under other. For `WEIGHTS`, `build-all.sh` passes `--no-config` with the registry name, and `build-model.py` then does not use `--default-weights`. Evidence quotes avoid source lines that hold a bar character. For that reason the `nixfmt` claim of `TRON_NIX_LINT_SHELL` (line 190 of `lefthook.yml`) and the exit status 2 of `TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT` (lines 36 and 146 of `perfetto/launcher-common`) have no quote. Two behaviours were confirmed outside the checkout with scratch commands: GNU make keeps an empty `UV` with `?=`, and bash 5.1.16 evaluates `0x` as 0.
